rules.source_statement: Chapter XLIX 'Of Marriage' begins below the divider after the preceding forty-three general horary aphorisms.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This heading belongs to Chapter XLIX, not the previous section.

rules.source_statement: First house/lord, Moon and Moon's separating planet signify the querent.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate the Moon's past separation from her later application.

rules.source_statement: Seventh house/lord and planet to which Moon applies signify the desired partner.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep spouse/querent roles directionally distinct.

rules.source_statement: When a MAN asks marriage, Lilly names the Sun together with Moon as additional significators under his historical gender-specific scheme.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not characterize these as proven innate or natural human roles; the source uses a historical conventional pairing.

rules.source_statement: For a female querent, Lilly adds Venus and Moon as natural significators.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical gendered convention only.

rules.source_statement: Ascendant lord or Moon applying to seventh lord predicts desire fulfilled with much petitioning and solicitation.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Direction first-to-seventh and labour condition essential.

rules.source_statement: Square or opposition with reception may accomplish marriage slowly with labour and trouble.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Both hard aspect and reception required, not a generic positive.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord applying to first lord, or Moon's applying planet to the separating planet, or seventh lord in ascendant, suggests easier marriage with sought partner's goodwill.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Opening paragraph begins original PDF336 and continues onto PDF337; include both original pages in locator.

rules.source_statement: A separately headed set of aphorisms is attributed to Alkindus concerning marriage.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly-mediated attribution, underlying Al-Kindi source uncollated.

rules.source_statement: Under Lilly's Alkindus attribution, ascendant lord applying to seventh lord is an argument marriage is performed; the printed margin adds the converse seventh-to-first application.
preconditions: Application of the specified first and seventh lords; the text does NOT restrict this item to trine/sextile.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The later discussion of trine or sextile must not be projected back into this broad statement.

rules.source_statement: Moon applying to Venus, with Venus strong and increasing in motion and in her own dignity, and the Moon likewise in dignity, is one Alkindus-attributed sign of completion.
preconditions: Venus is described as strong and increasing in motion and dignified, and Moon likewise dignified; Moon applies to Venus.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not shift Venus' motion condition exclusively onto the Moon.

rules.source_statement: Venus beholds Sun AND Sun has some dignity in the ascendant AND Sun beholds the lord of its own sign/dispositor; these are presented as a single marriage-completion testimony.
preconditions: All three conditions are joined by AND; the Sun's aspect target is lord of Sun's own sign, not the ascendant lord by default.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Earlier draft wrongly treated requirements as OR and replaced the Sun's dispositor with first lord.

rules.source_statement: If the applying planet and the planet it applies TO are both cadent, especially if their dispositors do not behold them, hopes exist at first but delaying and dragging may end with no marriage.
preconditions: An application EXISTS; both parties to it are cadent and dispositors' regard qualifies the verdict.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Earlier 'not regarding one another' reversed the first premise; this is not a judgment on no contact.

rules.source_statement: Under Alkindus, Moon, Sun, Venus and the lords of first and seventh in angles and mutually regarding (or beheld by their dispositors), even by hard aspect, are said to show initial despair but eventual marriage by consent of all parties.
preconditions: Named significators and angularity; mutual regard OR regard by their own lords, including possible square/opposition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Consent by parties and the alternative dispositor-aspect condition are source conditions, not evidence of actual consent.

rules.source_statement: Printed subsection 'Of Marriage, whether it shall take effect or no?' begins below the Alkindus aphorisms on original PDF337 and continues PDF338.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: It has a printed heading, although it is not a new numbered chapter.

rules.source_statement: New section repeats first lord/Moon/Moon's separating planet for querent and seventh lord/Moon's applying planet for the desired partner.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Includes sex-specific Sun or Venus supplements across page boundary.

rules.source_statement: In the section on marriage taking effect, seventh lord placed in first or applying to first lord is printed as the sought party consenting UNWILLINGLY, despite a neighbouring paragraph suggesting goodwill.
preconditions: Seventh lord in first OR applying to first lord; retain the original printed word 'unwillingly'.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source PDF338/printed304 explicitly says 'unwillingly'; no p304 erratum. This conflicts with p303 goodwill and could be a printer error, but no silent emendation is authorized.

rules.source_statement: Ascendant lord or Moon applying to seventh lord, or placed in seventh, is said to produce marriage through the querent's own labour.
preconditions: First lord/Moon applying to seventh lord OR in seventh; laborious completion is the proposed outcome.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not contrast this with an invented straightforward willing-consent implication from R1937, whose printed word is unwillingly.

rules.source_statement: When direct paths fail, translation of light between the signifiers is said to effect marriage via friends or acquaintances.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An actual translator between the relevant planets is required.

rules.source_statement: Moon in the TENTH is said to signify mediation by friends; Moon applying to Venus is another friend-mediated route, and Sun applying to Venus, especially when Sun has seventh-house dignity, likewise furthers marriage.
preconditions: Three printed alternatives: Moon in tenth; Moon applying Venus; Sun applying Venus with special Sun seventh dignity.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original reads tenth, not seventh, for the lunar placement. The Sun and Venus clause is distinct.

rules.source_statement: Lilly's alternatives include first lord in seventh, seventh lord in ascendant, or aspecting the LORD of the opposite house by good aspect; each gives encouragement for effecting the match.
preconditions: The first or seventh significator must occupy the counterpart's house OR behold the appropriate lord with favourable aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not collapse 'in seventh' into any unspecified 'other house'; the phrase 'or with the Lord thereof' is preserved.

rules.source_statement: When a man asks, his four cited significators are first lord, Moon, the planet Moon separated from, and Sun.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: These belong to the male-querent arrangement.

rules.source_statement: Woman sought in a man's query is signified by seventh lord, Moon's applying planet, planet in seventh, and Venus.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not confuse Moon-separated past planet with Moon-applied future planet.

rules.source_statement: When a woman asks, first house/lord, Moon, Moon's separating planet and Venus are hers, and seventh and Moon's applying planet are the man's.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Sex-specific source convention; not valid modern identity/relationship description.

rules.source_statement: First lord placed in seventh or seventh lord placed in first is one proposed marriage-completion route.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source compares these positions as alternatives.

rules.source_statement: A planet from which Moon separates applying to a planet Moon applies to is another completion mechanism.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Two nonlunar bodies transfer influence in the stated order.

rules.source_statement: Application between Sun and Venus is a separate natural-signifier marriage indication.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Specific application, not arbitrary astronomical proximity.

rules.source_statement: Mutual/interchangeable dignities, reception, translation or collection by a weightier planet may perfect marriage; the passage describes these as additional source testimonies.
preconditions: Actual dignity exchange or light/reception mechanism involving relevant signifiers.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source does not require prior failure of every simple aspect; previous draft added an unsupported exclusion.

rules.source_statement: Interchangeable essential dignities of the signifiers, explained in the printed margin as one in the other's terms and another in triplicity or similar, are proposed as a completion sign; across page turn the Moon in seventh gives virtue to first or seventh lord.
preconditions: Exchange of signifiers' dignities OR Moon in seventh transferring virtue to the appropriate first/seventh lord.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No Sun-or-Venus angular exchange appears at this location; earlier record invented it.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord in ascendant is read as the desired party loving most.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Reverse placement has opposite role.

rules.source_statement: First lord in seventh is read as querent loving most.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not verified psychological fact.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord in seventh, especially its own domicile, describes the desired partner as free from love, little minded to marry, and with the woman's or man's marriage portion known.
preconditions: Lord of seventh in seventh or own domicile as printed.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Both source ideas, freedom from love and portion known, are authorial guesses not actual wishes or finances.

rules.source_statement: Quesited significators not beholding querent significators are read as another love or aversion.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Two alternate readings, not proof of infidelity.

rules.source_statement: Frustration of a completing application is associated with marriage prevented by the planet causing it.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Obstructing planet must actually intervene.

rules.source_statement: Read a frustrating planet's house rulership and location for the attributed cause of obstruction.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The rule is conditional on an identified frustrating planet.

rules.source_statement: Second-house ruler helping transfer or collect light is said to represent a dowry or financial helper.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is mediation, not the independent money-shortfall obstruction.

rules.source_statement: Third-house ruler helping mediation is interpreted as help by a brother.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original family-role mapping, not independently identified.

rules.source_statement: Tenth-house lord in the mediation list represents mother.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep local context; later house-obstacle list differs.

rules.source_statement: Fifth- or eleventh-house lord mediating is associated with friend.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Either house suffices in source.

rules.source_statement: Sixth-house mediation may represent uncle, aunt or servant.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Multiple original alternative roles.

rules.source_statement: Original-volume erratum instructs deletion of the printed conjunction symbol from the marriage-aspect comparison. Thus SQUARE or OPPOSITION implies much ado; TRINE or SEXTILE eases completion; RECEPTION is best.
preconditions: A marriage otherwise promised by one of the specified aspects; the conjunction token is explicitly deleted by printed305 line22 erratum.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original PDF339 still prints the conjunction glyph; errata PDF888 says 'p305 l22 dele [conjunction]'. Preserve both witnesses and the approximate line-count difference.

rules.source_statement: Separate heading asks what will hinder the marriage and starts an interception/frustration procedure.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: New subsection on printed305.

rules.source_statement: Despite seeming probability of marriage, an EVIL planet may obstruct reception between signifiers, frustrate their intended aspect, prohibit it, or interject rays between them; inspect the evil planet for the alleged obstacle.
preconditions: Existing favourable marriage indications notwithstanding, a specifically harmful planet prevents reception, perfection, or interposes its rays.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original does NOT here call beneficial translation of light the obstruction; earlier draft reversed the mechanism.

rules.source_statement: The marriage may be broken on the QUERENT'S behalf when funds or fortune are lacking ON THAT SIDE, where the obstructing planet is lord of second.
preconditions: Second-house lord actually hinders the significators' reception; lack of money is attributed to querent's side.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer insufficient dowry of the quesited here; the text locates the deficiency on querent's side.

rules.source_statement: Third-lord obstruction is attributed to the querent's kindred, brother, sister, untoward neighbour or a journey.
preconditions: Third lord participates as frustrating planet in the marriage question.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source says 'some Journey', not necessarily a short journey.

rules.source_statement: Fourth-lord hindrance may indicate a parent refusing to agree, inability/refusal to part with lands/houses/tenements, or a parent who WILL SETTLE NO ESTATE.
preconditions: Fourth-house lord is the obstruction; parent/property categories are alternatives.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original says 'will settle no Estate', a refusal rather than demonstrated inability.

rules.source_statement: Fifth-house lord used as obstacle may raise objections about children if either party has any; in a bachelor question rumours or FEARS about fertility, prior offspring or sexual misconduct may be voiced, including scandal rather than established facts. Apply analogously if a woman asks.
preconditions: The fifth lord is the relevant hindering planet; distinguish child-present scenario from a bachelor's question and all claims as others' objections or fears.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source says 'perhaps it is objected', 'scandalized', and 'feared'; no actual infertility, offspring, infidelity or lechery is verified. 'Luxury' is historical sexual indulgence, not material luxury.

rules.source_statement: Sixth-house hindrance can arise from the querent's father's kindred, an uncle or a servant, or illness affecting the querent.
preconditions: Sixth lord as obstructing planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep the source's 'his Fathers Kinred' and alternatives; no medical assessment inferred.

rules.source_statement: A planet in seventh might point to another friend, public enemy, earlier quarrel or lawsuit hindering the match.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Several possible social categories, not proven accusations.

rules.source_statement: Eighth-lord as marriage impediment can mean death bereaves the QUERENT before marriage, or that the QUESITED lacks sufficient portion and their estate is disapproved.
preconditions: Eighth lord is obstructing; distinguish the affected querent and quesited parties.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author presents two outcomes; the record does not independently establish inheritance, an actual death, or deficient wealth.

rules.source_statement: Ninth-lord impediment can mean the QUESITED'S kindred, religious difference or an obstinate priest, or a long journey undertaken by the QUERENT.
preconditions: Ninth lord is the frustrating significator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The identities and who undertakes the journey are explicit and must not be reversed.

rules.source_statement: Tenth-house ruler as obstacle is linked to desired partner's father, querent's mother, a principal person, officer or magistrate.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from tenth lord in earlier help-by-mediator list.

rules.source_statement: Eleventh ruler obstructing is interpreted as friends of either party, sometimes even those first introducing the match.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Only applies where that ruler is obstructing.

rules.source_statement: Twelfth-lord obstruction suggests secret underhand dealings and slander against the QUERENT, who Lilly says may NEVER KNOW by whom the slander was privately insinuated.
preconditions: Twelfth lord actually obstructs the match.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source speculation; do not attribute actual secret slander to an unidentified real person.

rules.source_statement: Similar house categories may identify one who helps the querent when the relevant planet gives beneficial mediation.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Reverse application needs a helping, not obstructing, role.

rules.source_statement: Separate heading 'Whether a man shall Marry' introduces general yes/no testimony.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Section follows prior intervention causes on printed307.

rules.source_statement: Moon beholding Sun or Venus by good aspect, or mutual first/seventh lord placement or good aspect, is given as positive testimony for marrying.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source gives multiple alternative favourable testimonies.

rules.source_statement: Signifiers in prolific signs or Venus' dignities are additional pro-marriage testimony.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source says these strengthen prospects, not a measured fertility test.

rules.source_statement: Separate heading 'The time of Marriage' shifts from yes/no to duration.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not an independent couple or second prophecy.

rules.source_statement: Degree gap to applying Moon–Sun/Venus or first/seventh rulers is mapped to DAYS if movable, MONTHS if common, YEARS if fixed signs.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires particular application and source sign modality.

rules.source_statement: Lilly restricts that days/months/years timing method to strong marriage testimonies and SWIFT significators.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Without both prerequisites, the simple scale is not admitted.

rules.source_statement: A new subsection asks how many husbands a woman will have.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical gendered method, not verified marital history.

rules.source_statement: Arabic rule counts planets between degree of tenth cusp and Mars as proposed husbands.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires correct zodiac-longitude direction, not human observation.

rules.source_statement: If Mars is in eleventh, source instructs counting from Mars to Jupiter instead; other authors count Mars to tenth lord.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: These are rival source procedures, not necessarily interchangeable.

rules.source_statement: Lilly states plurality is better judged from seventh-house ruler, rather than treating Arabic planetary-count rule as universally best.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep authorial hierarchy and criticism of alternatives.

rules.source_statement: Common signs for Sun/Mars, many planets in seventh or Sun trine/sextile many planets in seventh are given as multiplicity indicators.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Plurality-of-husbands passage uses Sun and Mars wording associated with original-volume erratum printed307 line28 'r for [Sun glyph] and [Mars glyph]'. Body glyph is partially obscured and source-collation uncertainty remains.

rules.source_statement: Subsection asks from what part a person shall marry.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original printed308.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord in ninth implies marriage to a stranger.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires specified house placement.

rules.source_statement: First and seventh lords in same quarter, house or sign suggest a partner from nearby.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Alternative proximity indications, not a distance.

rules.source_statement: Seventh-lord sign and predominant quarter testimonies suggest a compass direction, with sign preferred to quarter.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No measured location or azimuth.

rules.source_statement: Moon with Venus is used to claim sought partner has agreeable traits.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Gender-stereotyped character allegation.

rules.source_statement: For the woman, Lilly judges by the planet the SUN beholds: SUN in trine/sextile of SATURN implies wise and painstaking/diligent; SUN aspecting JUPITER implies honest. A different earlier Moon–Venus clause concerns the man.
preconditions: Question concerns characterization of the woman and the Sun's trine/sextile to Saturn OR Sun aspect to Jupiter, separately.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Earlier draft wrongly put Moon with Mars and misinterpreted 'painfull' as causing pain rather than industrious/diligent.

rules.source_statement: Sun and Moon in square or opposition are said to indicate contention and separation.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires specific bodies and hard aspect.

rules.source_statement: Subsection compares which partner is 'more noble'.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Seventeenth-century status claim, not contemporary worth.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord in an angle and ascendant lord in succedent is read as woman higher-status; reverse favours man.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Relative placements determine direction.

rules.source_statement: Lilly's preferred way to compare spouses' alleged nobility is ESSENTIAL DIGNITY first, then, if no advantage there, WHO IS BEST PLACED IN AN ANGLE; he says same method compares companions or other persons.
preconditions: Compare relevant two significators' essential dignity first; use angularity only if that does not decide.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical class hierarchy not valid social worth; prior draft treated dignity and angularity as equal simultaneous criteria and omitted 'two Companions'.

rules.source_statement: Another subsection asks which spouse will be 'master'.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical power language, not moral recommendation.

rules.source_statement: When ascendant lord or Moon is received at an angle by a heavy/ponderous planet under the printed reception conditions, Lilly says THE QUERENT SHALL BE MASTER; other strength/dignity placements may indicate submission.
preconditions: First lord or Moon received by appropriate weighty angular planet; consider relative dignity/house placement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source's power inference is period social ideology, not relationship compatibility evidence.

rules.source_statement: Page309 continues whose significator is strong and whose is cadent/ill-dignified, associating the weightier partner with dominance and weaker with subjection.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation of p308, not separate patient.

rules.source_statement: The subsection 'Whether she be rich or not' begins an eighth-house financial judgment.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Works for partner's wealth, not a personal marriage-prospective outcome.

rules.source_statement: If eighth-house ruler or planet in eighth is strong or Moon applies to eighth lord by favourable aspect, Lilly judges partner wealthy.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Eighth house is considered counterpart's resources; condition of strength/aspect required.

rules.source_statement: If relevant eighth-house significators are weak, source suggests poor condition of partner's estate.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No actual audited financial information.

rules.source_statement: When a woman asks about a man's wealth, Lilly says to judge in the same manner and concerning HER estate as printed ('ead em est ratio' in Latin is given), without specifying an additional modern turned-house algorithm.
preconditions: Woman herself asks the financial question; apply the text's stated analogy.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed wording 'of her estate' is copy-qualified; earlier draft silently changed the person to man and invented a turned-house procedure.

rules.source_statement: Subsection 'Whether the Marriage be Legitimate' introduces challenge by an earlier partner or disputed obligation.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is an early-modern legal/social status claim, not modern validity.

rules.source_statement: If either partner's significators are vitiated or joined to Saturn or Mars WHEN THOSE PLANETS ARE NOT significators in the question, or are with the printed South Node ☋, Lilly calls the marriage illegitimate.
preconditions: Saturn/Mars status as NON-significator, or distinct South-Node condition, is essential.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: 'Unlawful marriage' is Lilly's historic label, not a modern legal determination; South Node glyph is legible in print.

rules.source_statement: First and seventh lords in trine or sextile are offered as testimony of agreement AFTER marriage; separately Moon beholding its own dispositor OR lord of exaltation by good aspect is given the same inference.
preconditions: These are separate alternative agreement testimonies, not Moon testimony only strengthening the first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not omit lunar exaltation-lord alternative or make house placement compulsory.

rules.source_statement: When NEITHER first nor seventh lord is angular, Lilly judges which spouse is more weighty/strong and would be master or strive for mastery; afflicted Sun is worst for man, afflicted Venus worst for woman, afflicted Moon bad for both.
preconditions: No angular placement of either principal lord for fallback comparison; planetary affliction clauses are sex-specific.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source uses 'or strive for it' and 'impedited' distinctions, not guaranteed dominance.

rules.source_statement: Separate subsection 'Disagree' opens lower page309 and continues on page310.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Structural marker, next source text to be included.

rules.source_statement: Original print across PDF343–344 includes first and seventh lords in square/opposition or an impeded Moon's lord beholding ascendant; Mars or a retrograde/combust planet in ascendant implies quarrels due to QUERENT; similar affliction to seventh lord attributed to desired party.
preconditions: Read earlier house-lord hard aspects and parallel first/seventh afflictions; source continues across page break.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No real person's moral responsibility is established from this 1647 system.

rules.source_statement: For a question asked by a MAN, Saturn, Mars or SOUTH NODE ☋ in ascendant supplies an additional historical argument of contention attributed to the querent or woman, following the Moon affliction clause.
preconditions: The specific ascendant placement and male-querent condition are source-essential.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Earlier draft omitted this explicit Saturn/Mars/☋ placement; do not apply as universal.

rules.source_statement: If the THIRD-HOUSE LORD is the planet afflicting or hindering and is IN ASCENDANT OR SEVENTH HOUSE, Lilly attributes the contention to brethren or kindred.
preconditions: Third lord both afflicts and occupies either of the named houses.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The house condition cannot be omitted or treated as a proven real-world culprit.

rules.source_statement: An infortune in tenth is taken as brawling and wrangling in the author's scheme.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not all tenth planets qualify.

rules.source_statement: An INFORTUNE IN THE FOURTH (following the tenth-house malefic example) is said to signify divorce, willingness to divorce, or hindrance concerning dowry.
preconditions: A malefic/infortune physically PLACED in fourth house, not merely fourth-house ruler afflicted.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Preserve all three alternatives; original draft omitted divorce and changed house placement to ruler affliction.

rules.source_statement: Unfortunate Moon beholding ascendant is alleged to bring brawling, separation or dishonest living.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source moral allegation without supporting social observation.

rules.source_statement: Malefics in fourth or tenth are said to bring quarrels involving parents or injurious people.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Need both ill planetary status and relevant houses.

rules.source_statement: If Moon's separating planet and applying planet do not connect by aspect, author gives an additional argument of contention.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Intervening relationship, not generic void course.

rules.source_statement: Moon aspecting OR conjunct Saturn or Mars in the specified conflict context is said to threaten quick death or misfortune; only when that CONJUNCTION is in tenth or fourth does Lilly add the masculine/feminine-sign assignment to which partner suffers.
preconditions: Moon aspects OR conjoins Saturn/Mars; 10th/4th conditional restricts the partner/gender attribution.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source speculates about death and conflict; neither has independent verified outcomes.

rules.source_statement: In 'Who shall be the cause of their Strife, or the authour of their Good', Moon TRINE or SEXTILE good planets predicts gifts from friends; Moon SQUARE good planets signifies benefit 'by dead men'; Moon CONJUNCT good planets suggests benefit by the spouses' own industry and labour.
preconditions: Specific lunar aspect to good planet: trine/sextile vs square vs bodily conjunction each carries different source outcome.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No opposition or quarrel outcome appears in this clause. This is historical money/benefit interpretation, not independently observed death or gifts.

rules.source_statement: An afflicted Moon, eighth/twelfth placement, or void of course is said to bring troubles, grief or sickness; if related afflicted planets are angular Lilly describes a PROBABILITY of separation OR long disagreements.
preconditions: Match each affliction and house case to its own branch rather than pooling simultaneous conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author says probability, not certain separation; the alternative prolonged conflict remains explicit.

rules.source_statement: The unnumbered heading reads 'THAT the Marriage shall be broken, and the cause thereof', not a question asking WHEN.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Heading spans source divider/passage; do not invent a timing test.

rules.source_statement: Although at present a marriage may appear VERY FEASIBLE, a heavily afflicted planet receiving the significators' light (square/opposition with ill planet, cadent etc.) is offered as cause of its later break-off.
preconditions: Initially feasible match, relevant light-receiver with specified adverse aspect or place.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not omit the initial feasibility contrast; source is author conjecture.

rules.source_statement: After interrupted engagement, Lilly compares which partner's significator remains strongest to infer who will marry another first.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Conditional on break-off, not a fresh unrelated natal marriage.

rules.source_statement: Ill planet hindering match as ruler of second or eighth indicates dispute over dowry or marriage portion.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: House rulers as alternatives, not both required.

rules.source_statement: Frustrating planet as third-house ruler is associated with brother as impediment.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not independently identifying a real family member.

rules.source_statement: Fourth or tenth lord as hindrance is attributed to father or mother, depending chart roles.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical family-role mapping, not a certain opponent.

rules.source_statement: If an ill planet carries/translates light between the signifiers and disrupts their union, the author instructs astrologer to DESCRIBE THAT PLANET to the party to warn about alleged mediator.
preconditions: Actual evil planet transporting light and causing break-off.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed source says describe planet; does not command identifying the actual person by house alone.

rules.source_statement: The Arabic aphorism concerns the Moon between the SEVENTEENTH DEGREE OF SAGITTARIUS and the FIRST MINUTE OF CAPRICORN: a woman who DEPARTS FROM HER HUSBAND or becomes widow is said never to return or remarry.
preconditions: Exact 17° Sagittarius to early Capricorn lunar range, plus separated-wife OR widow circumstance.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The printed margin warns not to credit Arabic aphorisms without other significators; no real return or remarriage verified.

rules.source_statement: The printed Arabic aphorism concerns Moon in the first TWELVE DEGREES OF CAPRICORN for one espoused to a wife: it says he will lose her before marriage, or die within six months, or live in discord with her.
preconditions: Moon in Capricorn 0°–12° AND a person espoused to a wife; three alternative author-reported outcomes.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The printed sign is Capricorn, not Virgo. Original margin cautions not to trust such Arabic aphorisms without corroborating significators; no mortality outcomes verified.

rules.source_statement: New subsection asks whether man or wife shall die first and at what time.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical sensitive claim only.

rules.source_statement: Compare first and seventh lords for which applies first to combustion: associated spouse is predicted to die first.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Exact directed comparative prerequisite, not any combust planet.

rules.source_statement: For a spouse alleged likely to die first, first-house lord retrograde/combust/in fall or NEAR LORD OF THE EIGHTH is applied to the man; like seventh lord to woman; afflicted SUN is worst for man, afflicted VENUS for woman.
preconditions: The near condition concerns lord of eighth, not merely the eighth house; map Sun and Venus gender directions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No patient mortality validation; the printed Venus glyph is slightly worn.

rules.source_statement: Lilly writes 'Usually I observe': the relevant significator first combust in TROPICK (cardinal) signs Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn is assigned a shorter time; common/mutable signs longer; fixed longest until alleged death.
preconditions: First combust significator and its sign modality; terms are historical Tropick versus common versus fixed.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a qualitative timeline with no calibrated elapsed years or observed lifespans.

rules.source_statement: Unnumbered heading 'Which of the two shall live longest' starts at foot of printed311/PDF345 and continues into PDF346.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Exact cross-page source boundary; do not start it only on PDF346.

rules.source_statement: In comparing the first and seventh lords to infer longer life, Lilly considers who is better placed, more essentially dignified, in good aspect to fortunate planets, and MORE REMOTE from the presence or evil aspect of the relevant EIGHTH-HOUSE LORD.
preconditions: Comparison of BOTH first/seventh signifiers and afflictions, including better fortune aspects and remoteness from eighth ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Comparative source prediction about mortality, not independent verification.

rules.source_statement: For the seventh-house partner the radical second is their turned eighth, so it serves as source death-house ruler.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not use radical eighth for both partners.

rules.source_statement: A subsequent historical subsection asks about alleged sexual virtue, framed by ascendant lord, Moon and Venus.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Period morality classification, not a valid contemporary assessment.

rules.source_statement: Lilly treats first ruler, Venus and Moon in fixed signs with helpful benefic aspects as evidence for a favourable moral judgment.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Gender-biased allegation only; not empirical evidence.

rules.source_statement: The presence of malefics, particularly Mars in a Venus-ruled place without reception, is cited as a contrary indication.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires specific conjunction/placement and reception.

rules.source_statement: In the earlier 'Maid or Chaste' section, MOVABLE signifiers aspected by infortunes are associated by Lilly with desire yet restraint: he explicitly says she refrains herself and casts off suitors. Separately a Moon/Sun relation with Mars is cited as another old character allegation.
preconditions: First lord/Venus/Moon as source-named, sign modality and infortunes' aspects; keep the contrary restraint branch.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The restraint statement is an important alternative to allegations; these are untested social stereotypes, not sexual history facts.

rules.source_statement: Lilly says such sexual-conduct judgments are not always to be trusted because, in his period language, 'the nature of women is changeable'; the same-volume erratum on p312 line17 directs reading 'it is NO GOOD to trust alwayes to this judgement'.
preconditions: Author's explicit warning against confidence in preceding conjectural rules.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep original gendered premise as an attributed historical claim rather than substituting gender-neutral authorial wording or endorsing it.

rules.source_statement: Under the 'Whether a Damosell be a Maid' passage, fixed versus movable/common ascendant and Moon sign configurations lead only to 'a doubt of Legerdemain'; the source additionally mentions SCORPIO ascending as an allegation she is or wishes to be overly familiar.
preconditions: First lord, Moon and specific sign modality or Scorpio rising, each as its own branch.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: 'A doubt' is an epistemic hedge, not a finding of any real conduct.

rules.source_statement: Lilly says he differs from some Ancients, citing MARS IN LEO with SCORPIO ascending as a case where the 'querent' is suspected and tempted but STILL HONEST.
preconditions: Mars in Leo and Scorpio ascendant; exact printed subject is 'querent'.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original 'is' lettering partly damaged. Do not silently change to 'quesited'; original PDF346, not PDF347.

rules.source_statement: In a later section the author associates fixed signifiers and favourable Jupiter/Venus aspects with favourable marital character assessment.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A historical, gender-biased conjecture, not proof.

rules.source_statement: Lilly claims first lord, Moon or Venus in fixed signs with fortunes give one favourable view, but then mentions MOON BEHOLDING MARS without qualifying 'adverse'; another branch where SUN and MOON are in NO ASPECT, nor Mars with them, describes suspicion but says NOT YET COME TO THE ACT.
preconditions: Check fixed/fortunate combinations separately from simple Moon-to-Mars regard and no Sun–Moon–Mars aspect case.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The printed negative 'not yet come to the act' limits the allegation; the margin adds Moon opposing Mars in specified sign pairs. Do not convert suspicion to fact.

rules.source_statement: The author instructs practitioners to be sparing in these inquiries and often remain silent lest mistaken judgments cause serious harm.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This explicit ethical caution must accompany all source allegations.

rules.source_statement: A subsection discusses allegations of a person having another romantic attachment besides spouse or partner.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical social question, separate from prediction of legal marriage.

rules.source_statement: In the following printed passage, if ascendant and Moon are both ANGULAR or in FIXED signs, Lilly says the woman is truthful and reports about her are FALSE; if first lord and Moon are fixed but the angles movable, she was tempted BUT GAVE NO CREDIT OR ADMITTANCE.
preconditions: Keep fixed/angular placements and alternative movable-angles branch, not a generic allegation.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source expressly denies the rumours and denies that she accepted temptation. This contradicts a broad misconduct reading.

rules.source_statement: If Moon is joined corporeally/by aspect WITHIN FIVE DEGREES OR LESS to SATURN, JUPITER, MARS or SUN, Lilly calls it a temptation by someone resembling the planet; the printed statement does not compare with separation beyond five degrees.
preconditions: Moon joining the source-listed planetary bodies within the five-degree angular bound.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The prior 'separation beyond the interval' contrast was invented, not printed. Historical character stereotype only.

rules.source_statement: Moon joined to VENUS or MERCURY is alleged by Lilly to mean a woman approached the person on another man's behalf, but she makes no reckoning of the older/younger go-betweens and laughs them to scorn.
preconditions: Moon physically joined Venus or Mercury in the source's subsection, with refusal and mockery outcome.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed outcome REFUTES compliance with solicitation, not evidence of an affair.

rules.source_statement: Another subsection asks whether a married woman has another relationship besides her husband.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical accusation category only.

rules.source_statement: First house/lord, Moon and Moon's separating planet are given as the husband's significators when he asks.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not confuse first/7th allocation when wife asks herself.

rules.source_statement: Seventh house/lord and Moon's applying planet signify the wife within that subsection.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source gendered role allocation, not independent identity inference.

rules.source_statement: Within the extramarital inquiry, the MOON AND LORD OF SEVENTH must BOTH be joined to LORD OF FIRST (through the specified reception or conjunction) for Lilly's favourable judgment: 'the woman is not faulty, but honest'.
preconditions: Both Moon AND seventh lord joined to first lord; reception or conjunction describes manner, not an independent loose alternative.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Earlier draft removed the both condition. The printed margin urges caution before negative statements about honesty.

rules.source_statement: Subsection asks about a woman's purported honesty, using lunar face, ascending sign modality and first lord.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Seventeenth-century judgment; no factual assessment of any person.

rules.source_statement: Moon in last face of Gemini is presented as an alleged adverse signal, subject to other placements.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not omit qualifiers or assert accuracy.

rules.source_statement: The printed alternative describes FIRST LORD OR MOON in MOVABLE or COMMON signs as allegedly adverse, while requiring BOTH the ASCENDANT and ITS LORD FIXED for the favourable overriding configuration.
preconditions: Adverse branch: lord first OR Moon in movable/common. Counterexample: ascendant AND its lord fixed.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original does not require 'weak' first lord or a separate 'dignified' requirement introduced by draft.

rules.source_statement: Moon in ascendant with Saturn can be interpreted as sexual contact by force and against the person's consent, not voluntary misconduct.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Critically preserve nonconsent; never equate victimization with wrongdoing.

rules.source_statement: Ascendant and its lord fixed despite Moon in movable sign can be interpreted favourably rather than negatively.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is an explicit counterexample to a simplistic movable Moon conclusion.

rules.source_statement: When the ASCENDANT is FIXED and first lord in fifth, OR Moon in fifth, OR fifth lord in ascendant, or stated corporeal joinings in a sign, the source guesses recent conception OR being lately tempted.
preconditions: Opening fixed-ascendant condition plus separate fifth-house variants.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Both potential conception and merely 'lately tempted' are alternatives; no pregnancy history verified.

rules.source_statement: Planets separated by roughly three degrees in the same scheme are offered as evidence an earlier concern may no longer apply.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source uses precise angular threshold and before/after distinctions.

rules.source_statement: Where seventh lord, Moon or both separate from ANOTHER planet BUT NOT LORD OF ASCENDANT, and separation is NOT ABOVE THREE DEGREES, Lilly supposes a prior outside attachment, now relinquished.
preconditions: Source named seventh/Moon separating planet OTHER than first lord, with 3° maximum separation.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation crosses PDF348–349; the claimed former attachment and its end are not observed.

rules.source_statement: If seventh lord or Moon joins MARS under the specified source condition, and the SOUTH NODE ☋ IS THERE, Lilly makes a separate adverse allegation about another attachment.
preconditions: Mars contact AND printed South Node at specified location; neither alone is enough.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original glyph on p315 line7 is blotted; same-volume erratum explicitly gives ☋. Not evidence about real person.

rules.source_statement: The LORD OF SEVENTH with the DRAGON'S HEAD ☊ is said to leave the woman BLAMELESS unless the lord is in conjunction with another planet, in which case Lilly separately distinguishes desires from conduct: 'if she be not faulty in act, she is in her desires and affections'.
preconditions: Moon/seventh lord source role and ☊ vs other-planet conjunction alternatives.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not conflate the favourable no-fault branch with an actual act; exact glyph ☊ is legible in original.

rules.source_statement: When MARS IS WITH THE SOUTH NODE ☋ and seventh lord joined as described earlier, Lilly says this DIMINISHES the alleged malice and that the woman has been hard pressed and persuaded, rather than willingly guilty.
preconditions: Mars with ☋ AND seventh lord joined in the earlier specified manner.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The printed p315 erratum corrects 'seventh'; this is not Mars/Node reception and the person is not proven to have consented.

rules.source_statement: If MARS with the seventh lord OR Moon is in ONE SIGN in the named source configuration, including South Node variant and one-degree distance, Lilly supposes a sweetheart in contract not far from the woman's house.
preconditions: Specific Mars/seventh/Moon one-sign contact and, for close proximity inference, within one degree.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source does NOT require angular house placement; physical nearness and purported contract are unverified.

rules.source_statement: Separation from Mars is used as a sign a previous attachment might have ceased.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep past and present distinct.

rules.source_statement: Lilly gives separate examples for MARS with seventh lord or Moon in Aries/Scorpio indicating earlier desire now diminished; and Moon LADY OF SEVENTH conjoined with MARS or JUPITER (one glyph uncertain) representing an allegedly higher-status man/bishop. Mutual reception indicates attachment still present but lacking opportunity.
preconditions: Identify which of the Moon-as-seventh-lady Mars/Jupiter conjunction, earlier Aries/Scorpio condition, or MUTUAL RECEPTION branch applies.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The planet in the second joining is copy-uncertain; no Saturn is named in this original PDF349 passage, contrary to the first draft.

rules.source_statement: Mercury joining seventh ruler or Moon is interpreted as a clerk, merchant or agile younger person.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires exact source signifiers/aspect.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord joined to VENUS, with reception or without aspect under the printed variants, is used by Lilly to say a woman cares not for men, but has friendship with women or speaks wantonly, while 'not naturally lewd or vitious'.
preconditions: The house ruler relates to VENUS alone under the given reception/trine/sextile or square-without-reception branches, continuing PDF349–350.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historic speculation about friendship, speech, orientation and conduct, not a factual judgment. Mercury is NOT present in this particular printed premise.

rules.source_statement: Seventh ruler or Moon with Saturn is associated with a supposed older, religious or sober person.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical stereotypes, not identified third party.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord joined to SUN signifies, by the quality of the DEMANDANT, previous attachment to a prominent person; WITH RECEPTION the person had or may have relations if desired, WITHOUT RECEPTION the person has forsaken her.
preconditions: Reception present versus absent between SUN and seventh ruler gives different source outcomes; questioner's quality affects social attribution.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source's personal-relationship allegations have no independent verification.

rules.source_statement: Additional planetary contacts with SUN, especially SATURN or MERCURY, are linked by Lilly to other supposed people, while saying she is 'somewhat tardy' and 'nor is she yet amended'.
preconditions: Planets must behold Sun together with seventh lord under source's printed circumstances.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: 'Tardy' may mean at fault/blameworthy in seventeenth-century use, NOT necessarily delayed; this is a qualified lexical inference, not certainty.

rules.source_statement: Separate section asks whether one's wife or lover has another 'sweetheart'.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source contains gendered assumptions; no scientific validity.

rules.source_statement: The printed 'If ones Lover or Wife hath a Sweetheart besides himself' paragraph contains DISTINCT planet-by-planet alternatives for a seventh-house occupant (not its lord): SATURN, JUPITER, VENUS, MOON, SUN and DRAGON'S HEAD, including several EXPLICIT DENIALS of an affair. Preserve those in source-review-added separate records.
preconditions: A planet physically occupying seventh which is NOT seventh lord, with each source-specific planetary alternative kept separate.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original draft wrongly flattened these into generic class judgement and lost negations; do not infer any actual relationship.

rules.source_statement: In the separate 'Hath she a Lover' subsection, the seventh lord void of course indicates no admirer under the stated context, with other node/source aspects handled distinctly.
preconditions: Apply the separate unnumbered heading's seventh-lord and lunar signifiers; no assumption that every seventh lord VOC entails real-world absence.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This record belongs after the new 'Hath she a Lover' heading, not to the previous 'sweetheart besides himself' paragraph.

rules.source_statement: In 'Hath she a Lover', seventh lord or Moon joined with Mars may, in the special source example, indicate a respected acquaintance WITHOUT dishonourable conduct.
preconditions: Seventh lord/Moon–Mars relationship in this source's class of inquiries.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a protective alternative against automatic allegations; follow the separate heading.

rules.source_statement: The preceding 'If ones Lover or Wife...' passage says analogous judgments can be made when a woman asks concerning a man, with corresponding signifier roles and house relations changed.
preconditions: A woman asks about a man, and significators are reversed relative to man's inquiry.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This source passage belongs BEFORE the separate heading 'Hath she a Lover', despite original draft ID ordering.

rules.source_statement: Late section asks whether marriage shall be perfected, assigning first lord/Moon to asker and seventh lord to sought party.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate heading, no new chapter.

rules.source_statement: In the late marriage-perfection section, first lord or Moon joined to seventh lord in seventh lord's dignities AND in ASCENDANT, ELEVENTH or TENTH (and HARDLY in SEVENTH) is given as possible positive sign.
preconditions: Marriage principal significators conjoined in seventh lord dignity AND source-listed houses, less assurance in seventh.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original named placement list and 'hardly in seventh' are essential.

rules.source_statement: Principal signifiers beholding by sextile/trine from stated houses, WITH OR WITHOUT RECEPTION and free from prohibition, frustration, abscission or retrogradation, give marriage perfection IF THE QUERENT PLEASE—Lilly explicitly supposes freedom of will in such a question.
preconditions: Sextile/trine with named signifiers and appropriate house, absence of intervening obstructions, and querent's freely choosing the match.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The express FREE-WILL conditional prevents astrology from supplying actual consent; include 'with or without Reception' as printed.

rules.source_statement: Square or opposition without reception is called failure; source contrasts hard aspect with reception.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Reception changes result, not generic hard aspect.

rules.source_statement: Square aspect between principal lords with reception is said to complete with difficulty.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not an opposition unless same source says.

rules.source_statement: Lilly expressly says against the ancients that seventh lord in first showed querent loves most, first lord in seventh showed sought person loves more.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Conflicts with earlier p305 interpretation; keep both with provenance.

rules.source_statement: A third planet translating influence via favourable aspect between unconnected signifiers may help effect marriage.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Specific translation/intervening planet required.

rules.source_statement: When identifying a mediating third party from the translating planet, the source says a MASCULINE AND DIURNAL planet denotes a man, while a FEMININE/NOCTURNAL planet can signify a woman or a man with a feminine constitution, and vice versa.
preconditions: A genuine third planet carrying benevolent influence between otherwise-unconnected marriage significators.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source's gendered planet categories are historical labels; prior Sun/Mars examples were not printed here.

rules.source_statement: Before relying on a translating planet, check if that planet or dispositor is retrograde, combust, unfortunate, cadent or in hard adverse aspect to an INFortune without reception; the phrase runs across the PDF351–352 page turn.
preconditions: Actual translating planet and its dispositor/aspect condition, NOT any planetary malefic elsewhere.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation includes 'square aspect to an Infortune, without Reception' on original PDF352.

rules.source_statement: Where those obstacles to the transmitting planet are ABSENT, Lilly positively says the marriage will be effected and continue, especially if the intermediary is a fortune.
preconditions: A genuine transfer/mediator exists and no specified obstruction occurs.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Earlier record's separate 'may fail' was a modern inference; source explicitly states only the favourable absence-of-obstacle branch.

rules.source_statement: New subsection asks whether a conceived child is offspring of the reputed father.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is historical paternity speculation, not a genetic test.

rules.source_statement: For that claim, ascendant lord/Moon represent interrogant, while eleventh house/lord are said to signify the issue in conception.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not silently replace eleventh with usual radical fifth; source says eleventh.

rules.source_statement: Favourable trine or sextile between relevant signifiers, with or without reception, is called supporting paternity.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source's eleventh ruler and identified parties required.

rules.source_statement: Square or opposition with mutual reception and perfect aspect may be treated positively.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Contrasts to hard aspect without reception.

rules.source_statement: First lord/Moon in fifth or fifth lord in first, without malefic obstruction, supplies another claimed paternity testimony.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Includes absence of evil aspects.

rules.source_statement: Fortunes regarding fifth house/lord are further claimed as supporting parentage.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source lists this as alternative corroboration.

rules.source_statement: ONLY IF NONE of the earlier corroborating conception testimonies apply, Lilly says Saturn, Mars or Mercury BEHOLDING the fifth house or its lord may give 'JUST SUSPITION' a child was conceived in adultery and the mother was 'STUPRATED'.
preconditions: No previously listed positive conception testimonies; Saturn/Mars/Mercury BEHOLD fifth or fifth lord without an invented aspect type.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: These are printed early-modern accusations under a source hedge, NOT genetic evidence or proof of assault or adultery. Do not silently translate 'stuprated' into a specific modern legal/medical term.

rules.source_statement: New subsection asks whether an estranged woman will be received back by husband or friend.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical reconciliation question, not relationship-safety guidance.

rules.source_statement: When the woman asks, Lilly explicitly makes seventh ruler signify the expelled or banished partner and first ruler the receiving party.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The direction of concern determines role; do not assign seventh to man by default.

rules.source_statement: Seventh lord for the expelled party beholding first house or first lord 'SO PARTILLY' and with true/good aspect is said 'WITHOUT DOUBT' to indicate eventual return and restored favour.
preconditions: Seventh lord specifically beholds first house or ruler, with the source's particular close/true favourable aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author's 'without doubt' overconfidence is faithfully recorded as historical assertion, not observed reconciliation.

rules.source_statement: If seventh lord does NOT behold the ascendant, an OTHER unimpeded planet can mediate only if the seventh lord BEHOLDS that planet AND that planet in turn BEHOLDS the ascendant; continuation runs onto PDF353.
preconditions: No direct seventh-to-ascendant aspect AND specific two-step seventh→intermediary→ascendant contact; the intermediary is not impeded.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Mediator is not merely any favourable planet present; page-break clause is essential.

rules.source_statement: An intervening friend is said to mediate reconciliation.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Requires a relevant chart-indicated intermediary.

rules.source_statement: Without mediator, Sun and Venus are used as supplementary significators in return inquiry.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical gendered planetary scheme.

rules.source_statement: Sun above earth and Venus in favourable sextile or trine to ascendant is read as easy return.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Both horizon and aspect conditions.

rules.source_statement: Sun below earth and Venus above with good aspect gives a slower return and neighbours' notice.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from preceding easy route.

rules.source_statement: Waxing Moon in good aspect to ascendant is said to show return after solicitation.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Increasing light and aspect required.

rules.source_statement: Waning Moon in second/last quarter, away from Sun beams yet beholding ascendant is said to show quicker/easier return.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Precise alternate to waxing Moon.

rules.source_statement: Venus occidental, retrograde and hastening to combustion is read as a woman regretting separation and wishing to return.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Compound timing and motion conditions.

rules.source_statement: After recent separation from Sun's beams, Lilly attributes regret to the man who caused wife to absent herself OR had ABUSED HER, while the woman may return angry, untrusting and 'NOR WILL SHE MUCH RESPECT HER HUSBAND AFTER THAT TIME'.
preconditions: The source context of Venus recently separating from Sun beams, as distinct from occidental/retrograde approaching combustion.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The text reports possible abuse rather than demonstrating it; retained disrespect is not a clinical/safety prediction.

rules.source_statement: Original PDF353 above divider closes XLIX; Chapter L on missing servants, animals and things begins below divider.
preconditions: Use the exact conditions embedded in the source statement, without adding modern assumptions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No Chapter L material admitted.

rules.source_statement: Printed heading 'Of Marriage' introduces a new significator allocation, separate from Alkindus aphorisms.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Unnumbered, not a new chapter.

rules.source_statement: Printed side heading 'It shall be' labels the five perfection routes, with a margin note about exchanged terms and triplicity dignities.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed side note is not handwriting; these are alternative testimonies.

rules.source_statement: Printed side heading 'Which love most, or desire it most' labels the first-versus-seventh lord attachment comparisons.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Heading rather than independently verified affection.

rules.source_statement: The author adds that other applying significators indicate more affection.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Applying direction matters; later printed317 has contradictory interpretation.

rules.source_statement: Printed subsection 'What manner of person he or she is' begins the period personality-characterization rules.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Handwritten annotations beside the heading are not Lilly's words.

rules.source_statement: Printed subsection 'How they shall agree after Marriage' precedes aspects, reception and the house-strength discussion.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not evidence of any observed marriage.

rules.source_statement: The preceding page begins a source clause about first and seventh lords in square/opposition and an impeded Moon-related ruler beholding the ascendant, continued onto printed310.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Cross-page original context and uncertain grouping must be retained.

rules.source_statement: Printed heading 'Who shall be the cause of their Strife, or the authour of their Good' precedes both discord and positive material help.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The gifts/benefits clauses are not all negative disagreements.

rules.source_statement: The source attributes its favourable character reading to a woman’s significatrix in own essential dignities, Moon in suitable reception/aspect, Venus in Leo without affliction, or Moon in Aquarius free of hard Mars aspects.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly says he 'found it ever true'; this is historical confidence, not measured accuracy.

rules.source_statement: Printed heading 'Whether a Woman be honest to her Husband' marks a new source section.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source-era moral category only, not a valid personal assessment.

rules.source_statement: The margin specifies Moon opposite Mars under Taurus–Scorpio or Libra–Aries pairings as an alleged adverse testimony.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Planet and sign pairings must be read as printed, not treated as verified conduct.

rules.source_statement: The source allows that someone may have been approached but declined and remained honourable, with common signs treated as less important in that branch.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Being approached is explicitly distinct from accepting an advance.

rules.source_statement: The text distinguishes Dragon's Head's earlier alleged error from a Dragon's Tail conditional about continued suspicion, with Mars reducing the asserted weight of blame.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Past and present, Head and Tail, and countervailing factors must remain distinct.

rules.source_statement: The author explicitly says Moon with Dragon's Tail can signify false reports of a woman, using the term 'slanders'.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The alleged accusation can be false; neither allegation nor denial is independently authenticated.

rules.source_statement: A first-house ruler combust in a movable sign is used in one source branch to discuss an encounter arising through force and lack of consent rather than voluntary action.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly's historical premise cannot be used to infer consent, culpability, or actual intimate conduct.

rules.source_statement: The printed margin qualifies this historical character judgment as applying when suspicion concerns the person asked about.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Print-margin scope note, not a source fact about any person.

rules.source_statement: The printed margin warns these claims need careful examination before declaring a woman dishonest or making a negative judgment.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Explicit source caveat against accusations; modern evidence for such inference is absent.

rules.source_statement: A seventh lord or Moon joined to the lord of ascendant's triplicity, or Moon separated from first ruler, is presented in one alternative as another friendship; by contrast seventh lord void of course is said to mean no other friend.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep the alternative conjunction, separation and void-course negative separate from the favourable 'both joined' clause.

rules.source_statement: The source separately considers Mars and seventh lord or Moon in Aries/Scorpio as implying earlier affection now diminished.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinguishes former from current speculation.

rules.source_statement: A mutual-reception alternative is said to show ongoing affection hindered only by lack of opportunity.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical relational allegation without evidence.

rules.source_statement: Mars in seventh, not its lord and not in its own sign, is given as one possible indicator of an outside acquaintance.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source speculation, not authenticated.

rules.source_statement: Saturn in seventh is said to signify a separate affection BUT without physical involvement.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not omit the denial.

rules.source_statement: Jupiter in seventh is used for a conjecture of difficulty maintaining fidelity.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No proven conduct.

rules.source_statement: Venus in seventh is said to create an impression of flirting, but the author explicitly denies the supposed offence.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Appearance is not conduct.

rules.source_statement: Mercury in seventh is associated with a former friendship that has already ended.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Preserve past, not present, source claim.

rules.source_statement: Moon occupying seventh is interpreted as no other acquaintance YET, with an unverified future allegation.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The explicit current absence must not be replaced by the conjectured future.

rules.source_statement: Sun or Dragon's Head in seventh is said to indicate no other friend or outside relationship.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a favourable negative-source branch distinct from Moon and Mars.

rules.source_statement: Printed heading 'Hath she a Lover' begins another inquiry AFTER the previous wife/sweetheart paragraph.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The first-pass draft merged parts of these two unnumbered sections.

rules.source_statement: A planet in seventh which is NOT its lord represents a possible acquaintance of its source-described complexion; if NONE in seventh Lilly says none; when a woman asks about man, use the related eleventh-house question.
preconditions: Use all source-named planet, house, aspect and role conditions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source explicitly requires excluding seventh-house lord and offers an absence branch; no affair is verified.
